blocks.text: The next afternoon, Seth walked along the lake after school. He kept well away from the place where Daniel had worked, looking for cables between the rocks.
A blue streak shot beneath the surface and circled back. Seth stopped. The glow reminded him of the water on the night of the flash.
“You came back!”
He looked along the empty shore. Then a fish rose in front of him.

It was round and blue-green, with dark perch stripes, yellow fins and enormous eyes. Barely a foot and a half long, it watched Seth with an eagerness that made him crouch beside the water instead of backing away.
blocks.alt: Seth meets the small blue-green Super Perch at the shore of Lake Erie.

blocks.text: “Did you just say that?” Seth asked.
The fish flicked its fins. “You understood me? I was hoping you would. You feel like the light.”
Seth glanced behind him again. Nobody was going to believe he had met a talking fish.
“How are you able to talk?”
“I can’t. People usually hear splashing. Only ones with power like ours can understand each other.”
Seth stared. The words were perfectly clear, although the fish’s mouth had scarcely moved.
“Super Perch,” the fish said, circling once. “I wasn’t like this before the light hit. Now even the big fish get out of my way.”
“It hit me too,” Seth said. Perch bobbed excitedly and swam closer.
“You’re the glowing light in the water!” Seth said.
Perch dipped beneath the surface and darted out in a bright blue loop. Seth grinned despite himself.

The speed made Perch hungry. He had started eating algae for energy, then racing through the cloudy water to see how fast he could go. Every lap left a clearer trail. By the time he noticed how much he had eaten, whole stretches of the lake had changed.
“You cleaned it?”
“I was trying to swim. And have lunch.”
Seth laughed. Daniel had taken credit for a fish’s lunch.
Perch’s fins suddenly stiffened. Farther along the shore, a motor started. He sank until only his eyes showed.

There was a device down there, he told Seth. Whenever it ran, the light inside him pulled toward its cage. He had escaped once by wedging himself behind a rock. Each time it came back, it reached farther.
Seth recognized the intake Billy had described. Daniel was trying to catch Perch, whether he knew there was a fish inside that glow or not.
“Stay clear of it,” Seth said. “I’ll bring help.”
“We should find out what landed in the water,” Perch said. “Before that man takes it.”
Seth looked across the lake, remembering the light falling from the sky. He had been so busy learning what had happened to him that he had barely thought about what caused it.
He promised to return. Perch slipped under the rocks, and Seth hurried to the nearest pay phone to call Billy. A robot was waiting for that power. Now they knew someone in the lake needed their help.
